Contrast material was detected1 in the intestines of twin neonates who were born 17 hours after iohexol was given to their mother for angiography, suggesting that transplacental transfer had taken place. 1. Moon AJ, et al. Transplacental passage of iohexol. J Pediatr 2000; 136: 548–9. Uses and Administration Iohexol is a nonionic monomeric iodinated radiographic contrast medium (see p.1474). It may be given intravenously, intra-arteri- ally, intrathecally, orally, rectally, or by instillation into body cav- ities and is used in diagnostic procedures including myelography, angiography, urography, arthrography, and visualisation of the gastrointestinal tract and body cavities. Iohexol is also used to produce contrast enhancement during computed tomography. Iohexol is usually available as solutions containing 30.2 to 75.5% of iohexol (equivalent to 140 to 350 mg/mL of iodine) and the dose and strength used vary according to the procedure and the route. Preparations USP 31: Iohexol Injection.
